summary: Regex engine documents how Bunzai runs a regex set in pure src/core/regex with no side effects. Rules are data executed as budgeted String.replace never eval or new Function; HTML-looking output only through SealedHtmlPreview and Risu cbs tokens stored then stripped before compile. The pipeline (`apply.ts`) runs applyRules in sortOrder with d-flag spans, per-rule and set budgets, condition chaining, overlay non-mutating matches, and firstMatchOnly, plus replace-ops group and case transforms. The AST layer (`ast/`) is a clean-room u-mode parser powering explainAst examplesFor analyzeRedos and dialect flag parsing. Travel honesty (`travel-lint.ts`) reports cross-platform lint for JS engines without forking parsers. The builder (`builder.ts` + `word-boundary.ts` / `word-family.ts`) turns word lists into verified patterns for Guided and Plain-words modes. Entity shape is entities/regex.md; platform phase truth lives in capabilities and platform-fields matrices, never as UI literals for pickers or the position-picker law itself. Execution now refuses unsupported syntax or flags and suspicious structures, checks substituted patterns, and bounds text and trace construction. Native matching still needs an external worker for preemption.

sections.title: The pipeline (`apply.ts`)
sections.summary: applyRules processes text and ordered rules deterministically. Match and capture spans come from the native engine through its d flag. It supports phase and condition gating, overlay results, first-match-only replacement and per-rule or set clocks. Structural admission applies after find-side macro substitution; shared limits bound text construction, capture counts, match enumeration and retained traces. A clock between steps cannot interrupt one native match. Studio callers add a terminable worker, whereas direct core callers do not acquire that deadline. Replacement operations implement numbered and named groups, match sugar, JavaScript dollar tokens and case transforms. Dollar tokens work in Bunzai but may become literal text in other engines, so travel lint reports the resulting portability risk. The linked safety page distinguishes logical limits, tested behavior and unverified packaged isolation.

sections.title: The AST layer (`ast/`)
sections.summary: The clean-room Unicode-mode parser produces typed nodes with spans and supports explanation, generated verified examples and structural backtracking reports. Explanation remains honest about ASCII word boundaries, and example chips must be confirmed by the real engine. Execution refuses both suspicious and dangerous analysis rather than treating suspicion as permission to run. Unsupported parser syntax or flags fail closed instead of using the weaker heuristic fallback. Stored v flags remain unchanged for conversion, but execution is refused until the analysis grammar implements them. Dialect parsing still preserves foreign flag tokens as data.

sections.title: Travel honesty (`travel-lint.ts`)
sections.summary: All five platforms execute JS RegExp, so divergence is a lint, not a parser fork. travelLint reports with spans: replace and flag extensions the destination will not run, engine-only rule fields, and host-age risks. The dollar-ampersand family reports on every lens but this engine's own, because it works while a rule is edited and breaks once it travels. The editor shows these dashed amber under Write-for; nothing is blocked or mangled.

sections.title: The builder (`builder.ts` + `word-boundary.ts` / `word-family.ts`)
sections.summary: Plain-words layer under Guided and Plain-words modes: word and phrase lists become pattern plus explanation plus execution-verified examples. Unicode-aware boundaries handle space-less scripts and the whole-word toggle drops out honestly where word-boundary would lie. Structure atoms cover numbers anything-between and line anchors. Round-trips through explainPattern which carries full AST reading for any parseable pattern.
